newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Hopeful India GDRs up with Bombay.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Hopeful India GDRs up with Bombay.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts posted steady gains on Tuesday amid optimism about prospects for a settlement of the country's political crisis and after an easing in monetary policy, traders said.
They said the market continued to trade on thin volumes, and this was unlikely to change until uncertainty over the future of the government and the 1997/8 budget was cleared up.
Trade was also seen dampened ahead of a holiday in India on Wednesday, and a further break on Friday.
Earlier on Tuesday, the Reserve Bank of India announced an easier credit policy, cutting the bank rate by one percentage point to 11 percent among other measures.
Also, the Congress Party's promise of renewed support for the United Front coalition under a different leader was seen supporting sentiment.
A broker said the majority of action on the GDR market was centred on Reliance, SBI and VSNL. VSNL gained 87 cents to $18.55/$19.55 and SBI was 150 cents higher at $21.75/$22.75.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 2.11 points, or 2.84 percent, up at 76.14 points, with the premium over the local market at 22.45 percent from 20.45 percent on Monday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index added 57.72 points to 3,647.44.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index made 2.03 points to 134.15, narrowing its discount to the local market to 3.72 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.15 points, or 0.24 percent, down at 64.45, a premium of 30.41 percent over the local market.
